blocks.x: Small appliances like toasters seem like such simple little gadgets, especially compared to all those multi-use toaster ovens. But here's my problem with toaster ovens: They take up a lot of space. Many are so big they can roast an entire chicken, which is great and all—until you need to try to find room for said toaster oven on your countertop. As someone who lives in a small New York City apartment and already has too many appliances for her own kitchen’s good (which is what happens when you test kitchen gear for a living), I’m well familiar with this conundrum.

That’s okay, though. While good toaster ovens can do a lot of different things, not everyone needs a countertop device that also broils, air-fries, and reheats a whole pizza while doing your son’s math homework. Sometimes you just need toast, and for that, a simple slice toaster is the best tool for the job.

Over the years, I’ve tested 31 toasters—cheap plastic toasters, techy toasters, aesthetics-first toasters. And my favorites keep things simple, the way a good toaster should, while also offering extra features here and there that enhance the toasting experience (yes, you can enhance the toasting experience). They’re relatively compact, sturdy, and easy to use. Most important, they deliver all the crispy, evenly browned carbs you want in the morning: pieces of toast, English muffins, frozen waffles, and bagels.

New in this update: We crowned the Amazon Basics 2-Slice Toaster our top pick for its superior performance at a low low price. We also tested the new Breville Eye Q 850 toaster to see if it’s worth the $300 price tag.
The best toaster for your money: Amazon Basics 2 Slice Toaster

Weight: 2.52 lb.

Settings: Browning levels 1–6, Bagel, Frozen, Cancel

The truth is, you don’t have to spend a lot of money to achieve perfect toast. In fact, the best toaster I’ve tried in all my years of testing rings in at about $20 and churns out evenly browned carbs done to your liking every time.

What we love: The price-to-performance ratio of this model can’t be beat. Amazon’s Basics line has had a few sleeper hits in our product testing over the years (their kitchen scale and stainless-steel pans, for instance) both here and at Epicurious , and this toaster continues to seriously impress me year after year. It drew even with our previous top pick, the Breville “A Bit More,” on practically every level, but at less than a fifth of the price, which is why I’ve decided to recommend it as the best toaster for most people. It’s got a lot of plastic on it, but given that fact it feels relatively well-constructed and has all the settings the average toast maker could need. Importantly, it also toasted bread evenly across all of the tests, demonstrating nice variation in browning across its six heat settings.

What we’d leave: Unless you need your toaster to feel fancy in addition to putting out great toast, there’s not much to complain about here. There was some slight unevenness in browning between the two sides of the slices of bread, but this was a commonality among most toasters I tested.
Best toaster for a pop of color: Beautiful by Drew Barrymore 2-Slice Toaster

Touchscreen buttons beep when pressed (a little annoying)
Beeps loudly when toast is done

Size: 11.06" x 8.11" x 6.57"
Weight: 2.97 lb.
Warranty: Limited 2-year
Settings: Browning levels 1–7, Bagel, Frozen, Gluten-Free, Cancel

What I love: Whoever’s designing the appliances over at Drew Barrymore’s Beautiful line seems to know what they’re doing. I was pleasantly surprised by this $40 toaster for its even browning, great variation in browning levels between each of its seven settings, and touchscreen interface that feels luxe for the price.

The Beautiful’s primarily stainless-steel construction feels sturdy and well-made, and it comes in 11 colors at the time of writing, making it a great choice for anyone looking to add a pop of pastel to their kitchen. The touchscreen interface (which is typically the kind of thing I’d only expect to see in a high-end toaster) lights up when you need it and turns off when you don’t. And, because the buttons are digital, the whole thing is easy to wipe down—no chance of pesky crumbs sneaking into crevices here.

In testing, the Beautiful toaster did an impressive job of toasting white bread to a distinctly different shade at each of its seven browning levels. It also handled bagels, sourdough, and frozen waffles with ease.

What I’d leave: While this toaster comes in more neutral colors like white and black, the look of the gold lever might not be for everyone. It also beeps quite audibly when you turn it on or press the buttons and when your toast is done. This is helpful for knowing that your bread is toasted when you’re across the kitchen scrambling some eggs, but it could be disruptive if you live with others in tight quarters.
The one that makes the best toast: Breville ‘A Bit More’
